blocks.text:
Breakfast, transfer to the airport and flight to Uyuni.

The Uyuni Salt Flat lies at an altitude of about 3,650 m and is considered the world's largest dried-up salt lake. During the rainy season, a thin layer of water turns its surface into an immense mirror, reflecting the sky and almost erasing the horizon. In the dry season, a white expanse of salt patterned with geometric cracks stretches into the distance.

The jeep route takes you through the train cemetery and salt fields. Old railway carriages stand in the open on the high-altitude plain, in sharp contrast to the empty landscape around them. Continue to Incahuasi Island, with its giant cacti, and see the Stone Forest.

As you travel across the salt flat, familiar landmarks disappear. The horizon is far away, with almost no trees or buildings around, so the sheer scale of the place is particularly striking from the vehicle.

Another stop is a salt factory in Colchani.

The route includes Palacio de Sal, a hotel built entirely of salt. The local dry, salty air is traditionally believed to benefit the respiratory system.

Lunch is served on the salt flat.

Afterwards, continue to a cave at the foot of a volcano, home to the approximately 800-year-old Coquesa mummies. Then stop in Tahua, where salt souvenirs are sold.

Overnight in the Uyuni area.
